meta.title: Finnish B1 Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1000 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Finnish → English (see the Finnish, recall the meaning) and English → Finnish (see an English meaning, recall the Finnish). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1000 words of Finnish for an intermediate learner, aligned to B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main points of clear standard input on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure, etc.' — a learner here is able to deal with most situations likely to arise while travelling, to produce simple connected text on familiar topics, and to describe experiences and events, dreams, hopes and ambitions, and briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Finnish has an examination graded to these levels (the National Certificates of Language Proficiency, YKI), but no graded word list for it was found published, so this deck is not an examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 296 of the 1000 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — work, money and the economy, education, the news, media and technology, government, law and society, the environment and the weather, health and medicine, travel and transport, the household and its chores, relationships and the stages of life, feelings and character, religion and festivals, ideas, reasons and plans, the connectors that join sentences, words for describing, and the verbs of thinking, deciding, arguing and changing — and the other 704 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Finnish, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every case of a noun and every form of a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Verbs are given as Finnish dictionaries give them, in the first infinitive (syödä "to eat", puhua "to speak"). The 483 nouns show their plural, their genitive, their partitive and their plural partitive, the forms consonant gradation and stem changes make hard to guess (käsi, kädet, käden, kättä, käsiä), and behind the All forms fold every case in both numbers; the 249 verbs show their "I" and "he, she" forms, their past and their perfect (syödä: syön, syö, söi, on syönyt), and behind the fold the present, the negative, the past, the perfect, the conditional and the imperative by person, and the passive. The Finnish Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters and their sounds. Real example sentences come with 992 of the 1000 words, three apiece for 947 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.

"You see," he explained, "I consider that a man's brain originally is like a little empty attic, and you have to stock it with such furniture as you choose. A fool takes in all the lumber of every sort that he comes across, so that the knowledge which might be useful to him gets crowded out, or at best is jumbled up with a lot of other things, so that he has a difficulty in laying his hands upon it. Now the skilful workman is very careful indeed as to what he takes into his brain attic. He will have nothing but the tools which may help him in doing his work, but of these he has a large assortment, and all in the most perfect order. It is a mistake to think that that little room has elastic walls and can distend to any extent.
